what_went_well: You spotted straight away that 2x is the common factor in 2x^2 - 8x, which is exactly the right first observation and earned you a mark on c1. Your handling of what was left was clean and accurate: from x - 4 = 0 you got to x = 4 without any slips, and that root is correct. The working is also set out clearly step by step, so it was easy to follow your reasoning.
what_went_wrong: At Step 2 you divided both sides by 2x instead of factorising it out. Dividing by x is only valid when x is not zero, so that step quietly assumes x cannot be 0 and throws that solution away — which is why Step 4 gives only x = 4 and c2 scored 0. Your note at Step 5 shows you suspected there might be more to find, and there was: the equation has a second root, x = 0, which your method had already discarded.
how_to_improve: Whenever the unknown appears in a factor you are tempted to divide by, factorise instead: write 2x^2 - 8x = 0 as 2x(x - 4) = 0, then set each factor to zero in turn to get x = 0 and x = 4. Build the habit of checking, before every division, whether the thing you are dividing by contains the unknown — if it does, rearrange to make one side zero and factorise. As a final check, count your roots against the highest power of x in the equation, and go back to your factorised line if you have fewer than you expect.
